messages.subject: RMySQL Connection
parts:
Hi,

I am building a R Shiny Application for operational Dashboard.

I have to access 7 different database. So I have created 7 connection.


log_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(), user='root', password='******', dbname='rtest')
data_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='******',dbname='raw_data')
score_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='******',dbname='score_data')
dev_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='******',dbname='dev_data')
val_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='******',dbname='val_data')
pmodel_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='******',dbname='pre_model_data')
view_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='*******',dbname='all_views')

I have put all the connection outside the server function in server.r

My program  structure:

log_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(), user='root', password='******', dbname='rtest')
data_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='******',dbname='raw_data')
score_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='******',dbname='score_data')
dev_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='******',dbname='dev_data')
val_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='******',dbname='val_data')
pmodel_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='******',dbname='pre_model_data')
view_con<-dbConnect(MySQL(),user='root',password='*******',dbname='all_views')

shinyServer(function(input, output,session) {

function1{

dbFetch(dbSendQuery(view_con,qr)

}

function2{

dbFetch(dbSendQuery(view_con,qr)

}

}

As I have to fetch data from all 7 databases through these 7 connection  multiple times in my program .
How to close the connection each time after sql operation & reconnect it so i can use it for next time ?
also the database performance can be improved?

messages.author: d6ebe55625e8e5a2
messages.subject: Re: RMySQL Connection
parts:
Take a look at the pool package; intro here: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/pool-basics.html and repo here: https://github.com/rstudio/pool

It may also be useful for you to look at the dbplyr vignette (http://dbplyr.tidyverse.org/articles/dbplyr.html) so you can use dplyr to query databases. You can even use dplyr + pool: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/pool-dplyr.html
